name: Jaguar XJ13
description:
The Jaguar XJ13 is one of motorsport's most tantalizing "what ifs" - a stunning mid-engined prototype built to return Jaguar to Le Mans glory, but destined never to race. Only one example was ever constructed, making it among the rarest and most valuable cars in existence.

Following five Le Mans victories between 1951 and 1957 with the C-type and D-type, Jaguar sought to reclaim their endurance racing crown. In 1964, as Ford and Ferrari began their legendary battle, Jaguar's competition department in Coventry began work on an all-new challenger powered by a revolutionary dual overhead cam V12 engine.

The Claude Bailey-designed 60-degree V12 was essentially two XK straight-six engines sharing a common crankshaft. With Lucas mechanical fuel injection, it produced 503 horsepower at 7,600 RPM and 518 Nm of torque at 6,300 RPM. Power was transmitted through a ZF 5-speed manual transaxle.

The XJ13's breathtaking aluminum bodywork was penned by Malcolm Sayer, the aerodynamicist behind both the C and D-type. Unlike contemporary prototypes with Kamm tails, Sayer created a flowing, pointed rear end featuring E-type-style lights. The aluminum monocoque chassis incorporated the engine and gearbox as stressed members carrying the rear suspension.

Working with minimal budget and staff, the small team completed the first car in March 1966. Testing began at Silverstone and MIRA through 1967, with the XJ13 reaching 195 mph despite weighing 1,040 kg. Then came devastating news: the FIA announced a 3-liter engine limit for 1968, rendering the 5-liter XJ13 obsolete before it could ever compete. The sole surviving example remains one of the most beautiful racing cars never to turn a wheel in anger.
author: Lucas Macedo & Team WSC Legends
